desc:
A small copse of birch trees surrounds a waterhole that provides sustenance to
fauna in the area; trails made by deer and small mammals converge to this place
from the surrounding plains. This permanent source of water allows for a lush
grass cover that provides smaller mammals with shelter. Several shrubs are
scattered among the trees; laden with berries they make ideal food sources for
birds and other small animals.
name: A Copse of Birch

desc:
On the ground the grass seems healthy; dry ears with spikelets consisting of
some florets raise above the green level of the leaves. The purple flowers of
thistles add colour to the surrounding landscape. Some animal tracks, marked by
droppings in the flattened grass lead to the east where a few birch trees
decorate the horizon.
name: The Purple Plains

desc:
The willow saplings have been planted close together in the fertile soil.
Crowded in such a dense grove, the willows have grown straight and tall with few
side branches at all. Some open spaces in this miniature forest and piles of
neatly stacked branches north near a trail indicate recent harvesting of some of
the year-old saplings. To the south the young trees are replaced by older
knotted ones.
name: Willow Saplings

desc:
The trees in the southern marshy part of the willow fields are very old, while
to the north on dryer ground the trees seem younger and healthier. Thick crowns,
spanning several feet sit on top of the thick short trunks. From these crowns
thin branches make the top of the trees look like giant hedgehogs. At the shade
side of the willow trunks brown fungi decorate them. To the south and west
wetlands border the forest.
name: Old Willow Fields

desc:
Lush grasses cover these fertile fields which stretch south and east. While
birds and small mammals seem to make up most of the animal life, hoof marks form
the evidence of grazing by large mammal. Occasional ash and birch trees dot
these plains, providing shelter for sparrows and other birds that can be seen
flying about. To the west the grasses are replaced by fields of old willows.
name: Open Grassland

desc:
These rich grasslands stretch west and south, the tall grass carpet broken only
by the occasional birch or elm tree. Shrubs and a small patch of willow trees
surround a small depression filled with muddy water containing small larvae and
bugs. Trails left by large animals feeding on the leaves of these shrubs are
marked by dried droppings and grazed leaves. To the northeast the gloomy eaves
of Mirkwood can be seen in the distance.
name: Depression in the Open Grassland

desc:
Luxuriant grasses cover the extent of this tilted grassland. Scattered among the
grass small woody shrubs with crimson and yellow flowers grow, filling the air
with their scents. In the low southwestern part of this grassland tall cattails,
with staminate flowers rising above the leaves, grow between the grass hinting
at a soggy underground.
name: Wet Grassland

desc:
Soot covered walls are all that remains of this small village. Once a place for
farmers from the surrounding areas to gather, it seems to have been abandoned
for many years now. Weeds and bracken have spread past the gardens surrounding
the derelict buildings, adding to the sombreness of the location. A few small
animals scurry among the debris, seeking cover from some unseen threat.
name: An Abandoned Village

desc:
Thick bushes grow among the grasses in this stretch of the plains. Some twisted
animal paths can be clearly distinguished, interweaving among the tightly packed
bushes. The ground slopes downwards slightly to the north leading to a soggy
area. Scattered among the bushes a few slender plants with bluish petals grow.
Small animals scurry about, alert to the slightest sign of a predator. Some
buildings have been erected in the distance to the south.
name: Plains North of a Village

desc:
Lush, green grass now covers the abandoned fields that lie next to the village
in the west. The earth rises slightly to the south, elevating as it turns into
vast grasslands. To the northeast, hills rise above the plains providing the
most salient landmark in the terrain, as well as a vantage point over these
extensive plains.
name: Grassland by the Village

desc:
The battered fencing that surrounds these fields is the clearest evidence that
whoever claimed ownership of them has long ago given up. Thistles, scattered
shrubs and bushes grow sparsely in the area covering up any other evidence of
farming activity. To the east a tall hill rises above the plains while to the
southwest the remains of a small village dot the horizon.
name: An Abandoned Field

desc:
This lush valley has a rich vegetation dotted with many different coloured
flowers. This provides an environment that is favoured not only by large grazing
mammals but also by small rodents and insects. A few scattered bones suggest
that predators also find an occasional meal in this location.
name: A Flowering Vale

desc:
Navigating these hills requires not much climbing. Sparsely distributed along
the hillside oak, ash and birch trees grow and among these several shrubs and
bushes. To the east the ground rises, while the northern and southern slopes
lead to small valleys in the plains. Among the bushes a worn trail indicates
significant transit of some large animals into a small creek among the hills.
name: Lightly-wooded Hills

desc:
These fertile plains show a increased number of birch and oak trees as the
terrain slowly rises towards the south into the hills. In addition to the trees
a few small bushes and shrubs provide food and shelter to a variety of small
birds and mammals. To the east the terrain slowly rises to the sky before ending
abruptly at a steeply declining rock face, preventing travel in that direction.
name: Lightly-wooded Plains

desc:
The grasses, richly coloured with flowers, grow abundantly in these fields,
providing a perfect habitat for insects and herbivores like deer and wild sheep.
Some stones, covered with moss, stick out between the grasses covering this
field. Just above this moss, small capsules carrying spores weave in the wind.
To the west the grassland drops significantly showing some small pools.
name: Grassland

desc:
Lush grasses cover these fertile fields which stretch north, east and south.
These grasses are filled with insect life that provides ample sustenance to the
birds that fly overhead. Several trees and shrubs grow, scattered across the
landscape, providing roosts for these birds and hiding places for other small
animals. To the southeast a hill rises, towering over the plains.
name: Open Grassland

desc:
Lush grasses cover these fertile fields and those that stretch west and north.
While the thriving insect life provides ample sustenance to small birds and
mammals, the sparse bushes and shrubs provide little protection from predators
and inclement weather. Southwards a lightly wooded plain leads to some rising
hills.
name: Open Grassland

desc:
The grassland in the east is replaced by wetlands with small pools whose banks
are covered by spike-rush, with tiny flowers at the top, and long reeds. The
wetland itself consists mostly of thick floating mats of slender sedge
characterized by bare stems with very long, very thin leaves. On the thicker
parts of this floating surface some orchids dye the landscape purple.
name: Wetlands

desc:
A thin layer of soil covers the barren, rocky ground. While some spots are
totally bare, other places are covered by grass and dark green bushes. Here and
there are nasty, rough rocks sticking up from the ground, making travelling
quite slow and unpleasant with their sharp edges. Underneath the sparse bushes,
tracks of small animals criss-cross the soil before disappearing into the small
holes between the rocks.
name: Uneven Plains

desc:
Half of the plain is completely covered by bushes and dense vegetation, whereas
the other part has been charcoaled by a devastating fire. Shrubs and bushes to
the east have been eradicated entirely, and only a few large rocks and stones
stick up from the burnt ground. An extremely steep slope leads to a bare valley
to the south. There are no visible paths around, which makes the movement
difficult. Behind the valley, magnificent hills can be seen.
name: Charred Plains

desc:
Short, yellow-green grass grows on the bottom of the valley with several rocks
and spiny bushes covering the ground. Steep valley walls rise abruptly, and
cliffs on the northern wall are especially filled with loose rocks and boulders
which make it too dangerous to proceed in that direction. A narrow but flat
valley floor slithers among the rocks and continues in every direction but
north. A majestic hill stands proudly in the south.
name: Dangerous Valley

desc:
This small, steep valley lies between the high hills and vast plains. The ground
is rocky and quite barren, offering easy access in all directions but the north,
where the valley wall is too dangerous to travel in. A fire recently spread
through the northern plains, carried by a wind and dumping ash, covering parts
of the valley with death-like greyness.
name: Steep Valley

desc:
The top plateau of the Great Hill is small, rocky, and contains a very limited
amount of low bushes and stunted grass. The wind has no obstacles here, and it
occasionally blows hard, making the sparse vegetation of plateau to bend. The
plateau offers a truly magnificent view of the surrounding areas. Looking
around, slopes and valleys encircle the hills from all sides. Looking beyond
those, vast plains continue in all directions as far as one can see.
name: Great Hill

desc:
This deep valley lies peacefully beneath an enormous hillside, beckoning the
travellers to settle down upon it. The towering hill completely blocks the view
northwards. The inclined, rocky wall makes a perfect home for a great number of
birds, and some of them can be seen circling the sky. A tiny path runs through
the elevating plains to the east and west, peacefully winding in the shadows
cast by the high hills.
name: Valley in the Plains

desc:
The sloping ground inclines gradually throughout the whole area. The surface of
the ground is rather grim: dark, grey stones are scattered around the slope, and
the short, stunted grass does not offer much comfort to passing travellers. No
trees are visible on the slope, as a narrow path can be seen descending from the
northern hills towards the more fertile lands to the west. To the east, the
ground is too steep and rocky for travelling.
name: Sloping Plains

desc:
High on the hills, an old path slithers through the rough terrain, descending
dangerously towards a slope in the north. There are rocks, stones, and boulders
on both sides of the path, which limit the view from here. There are some old
tracks on the path and the blackened remains of a few abandoned campfires.
name: High Hills

desc:
The slope is growing with thick, but relatively short, green grass. The incline
starts from a broad valley a few miles to the north, and then elevates steadily
throughout the whole region, towards the steep slope of an enormous hill in the
south. To the west, the ground descends abruptly into a rocky valley, allowing
no access. A small path winds down from the hill, turning around some grey
boulders, and leading to a junction which is visible from the east.
name: Sloping Plains

desc:
A rocky valley is resting at the foot of a majestic hill. The steep edges of the
valley rise upwards towards the sky as the end of the valley gets closer. The
valley ends at a round clearing, which is surrounded by a sheer rock face from
all directions. Brown rocks form an impassable hillside, covered with small pits
and black narrow hollows. Far above, few bushy trees have managed to grow on the
vertical surface.
name: Rocky Valley

desc:
Grey rocks and withered bushes are scattered over this rather flat plain. The
western side of the plain has a slightly higher elevation, where the terrain is
slowly rising towards some high hills that are visible to the southwest. Several
paths meet each other here, forming a small junction. A huge rock rests solidly
in the middle of it, with three arrows carved upon it. There are no signs of
life anywhere, except for a few old fireplaces along the path left by
travellers.
name: Meeting of the Paths

desc:
This flat plain is covered entirely with tall, dense grasses, which sway back
and forth as a cold breeze passes by. There is a small path slithering through
the thick, rolling fields. The landscape is dominated by high hills, which can
be spotted not far to the west. The open plain continues in all directions, with
the exception of the west, where a steep incline, filled with boulders, prevents
any further travel.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
The barren, flat plain is covered with tangled, yellowish grass tussocks. Large
areas are entirely dry, where grass is coloured almost orange. Only a few trees
are visible on the whole plain, and every single one of them looks grey, dry,
and dead. A huge hill is visible to the northwest, but a steep ridge blocks the
direct route there, forcing travellers to use a detour.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
The feral plain opens up in all directions. The ground winds up and down,
forming small mounds. The surface of the plain is covered by messy, bright green
bushes, and light grey, nearly white, stones, which are strangely grouped
together into small piles. Some high hills can be spotted to the west, whereas
the plain seems to end further to the east where it gets progressively rocky.
name: Rocky Plains

desc:
A foot long, brown-green grass covers the plain, forming a slowly winding sea
around the clumps of thick bushes that grow in great numbers around the area.
The eastern part of the plain holds vegetation so dense, that it is impossible
to go any further in that direction. A large number of small stones forms the
remains of a rarely used path through the field, which cuts the sea of grass
into separate areas.
name: Brushy Grassland

desc:
Dense foliage and a thick growth of low shrubs covers the plain, forming a wild
mixture of both deciduous and evergreen plants. The vegetation opens up just
enough for a wagon-wide path to clear through the field. The western parts of
the plain are more rocky, and a steep valley prevents those who pull themselves
through the bushes to pass by any further.
name: Bushy Plains

desc:
A fire has burned down most of the vegetation, only grey ash and charred, black
branches remain. A path leads through the fields, it is not very wide, and at
some regions it is hard to find under the windswept shrubs and ash. The land to
the north has been untouched by the fire, and has the look of cultivated
farmland. The eastern terrain is filled with sharp rocks and charred bushes,
making it impossible to travel there.
name: Path through the Charred Plains

desc:
The plain has been completely consumed by a raging fire. As the flames died out,
they left behind a few charred bushes, sooty stones, and a large amount of dark
grey ash. The landscape is otherwise flat, except for to the south where the
charcoaled plain transforms into a steep, dangerous-looking slope which descends
abruptly into the rocky valley below.
name: Charred Bushes

desc:
The grass grows sumptuously on the field, which contains the old remains of
beets, carrots, and potatoes. The field is divided by an ancient, weathered
fence made up of old, grey poles and rotten planks. The majority of the planks
have come lose from the poles, and now lie rotting under the grass. A few old
reinforced mangers, made of thick oaken beams, are still standing on the fields.
name: Abandoned Fields

desc:
A small, dusty path, covered with old footprints, courses between the fields.
The western field has been retaken by high grasses, bushes, and other plantlife.
Here and there, a pole from a former fence is visible in the middle of this
feral wilderness. A small ditch separates the eastern wheat fields from the
path. A wide track of fallen wheat is visible on the field, it looks as if some
big animal has wandered through the crop.
name: Path through the Fields

desc:
The brown plain is covered with bushes. A small path runs through the terrain,
almost completely hidden by all the thorns, leaves, and branches. At the
southern end of the plain, a path travels through a minor dip. Dense bushes are
blocking the way to the east and south, and the bushy plains continue onwards to
the northwest.
name: Path through the Bushes

desc:
Thick thorn bushes surround a small, windy path that is partially visible from
all the dead branches that cover it. Something seems to be rustling among the
surrounding thorns, making the vegetation move. The northern and western parts
of the field are completely covered with sharp thorns, allowing travellers to
only move to the east and south.
name: Bushy Plains

desc:
The scrubland is a tangled mess of feral bushes and small trees, which have
grown together with long, dry weeds. Parts of the shrubbery have formed thickets
so dense that the slithering old path heading south has become half-buried under
the vegetation. Thorny shrubs seem to continue on all directions, making
navigation through these plains restricted.
name: Path through the Tangled Bushes

desc:
With no other way out of the deep vegetation than to the north, the path ends at
a stony clearing within the shrubbery. The dense thicket encircling the path
makes it impossible to penetrate through, or view beyond, towards the
surrounding area. This seems like a good place for travellers to settle down for
the night, as it provides shelter against the strong wind that often crosses
these plains. Several deep tracks can be seen in the grass, maybe left by mounts
and wagons of other travellers.
name: End of the Path

desc:
Shrivelled grasses, bushes, and small plants are located all over this flat
plain. The terrain has been under drought, keeping the plants stunted. A few
noises that can be heard are coming from the small insects that fly by. The
rocky ground to the north and west hinders travel there, while the plain
stretches out elsewhere seemingly endless.
name: Withered Plains

desc:
This infertile and desolate plain extends a great distance eastwards, allowing
the wind to blow harshly through the area. Stones of various sizes and types lie
on the ground, especially to the north, where the plain seems impenetrable due
to the sharp rocks and stones. The plains are riddled with cracks among the
short grass, where the mud has hardened and split due exposure from the
elements.
name: Withered Plains

desc:
Dry, yellow-brown grass covers the central parts of this wide plain. The sea of
short straws is bent and cracked from the occasional gusts of wind that has
blown across this shrivelled landscape. Brush and thick bushes border the
windswept plain to the south and west, blocking the passage effectively, while
the plains extend in all other directions.
name: Withered Plains

desc:
The grassland peters out in this gaunt, windswept landscape. Everything is very
dry, and there are a few large blackened areas, where all the grass and other
undergrowth have totally been burnt away. A few bare trees are still standing on
the field, their trunks twisted and blackened, and their leaves having
shrivelled and fallen off. This bleak barrenness continues to the north and
west.
name: Arid Plains

desc:
This bleak plain is barren, containing only some modest vegetation, as even the
most adaptable flora has difficult time trying to gain a foothold in this dry
terrain. Some sandy brown and light green coloured, dried bushes still exist,
growing among the stunted grass tufts. The soil is withered as far as the eye
can see, and cracked in several locations.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
This extensive tract of uncultivated open land is covered with herbage and low
shrubs, like raspberries, brambles and spiky bushes, which form occasional
bright green spots in the otherwise somewhat insipid undergrowth. The terrain
looks modest, and harmless. Several foot-high fertile grasses surround this
peaceful plain. To the east, the grasses grows gradually longer, and have a
browner hue.
name: Tranquil Plain

desc:
This is a large, rocky area composed of narrow passes between steep rock faces;
coarse cliffs filled with dense briar thickets; and rounded boulders exposed by
erosion. Some of the rocks are half-buried in the ocher clay; some of them are
laying upon each other in dangerous looking, unbalanced manner. There are deep
burrows among the rocks, making it perilous to proceed further between the
boulders. The only easy way out is the green plain that is visible to the east.
name: Rocky Area

desc:
Vegetation in the area is primarily low bush and scrub. The land is mostly
without trees; instead a lot of tall, yellow grass grow here. Amongst it,
occasional patches of foot-high green grass make the landscape look vivid and
colourful. No clear path exists in any direction; on the other hand, the terrain
is so easy that pasturing animals can just wander wherever they want.
name: Plains of Yellow Grass

desc:
Various vigorous, shrubby plants dominate this area, blooming in rich shades of
yellow, orange, red, and crimson. Around them, large blue and deep purple
flowers make vivid colour patches that stand out from the mottled undergrowth,
which is painted in uncountable slight variations of green, brown, and even
grey.
name: Colourful Plains

desc:
The terrain is a verdant grasslands, with a few scattered clumps of trees and
bushes growing here and there. Rising from the lush grass, a long, rocky
escarpment dominates the area to the east, creating an impassable stony wall in
the otherwise featureless terrain. A few boulders are planted at the foot of the
rock wall, which looks so worn that the new boulders may fall down at any
moment.
name: Rocky Escarpment

desc:
An overgrown ruin, half buried in the high grass, stands within a bushy thicket.
A long time ago, there was a partly wooden barn standing on a firm foundation of
stones. Now, the building has collapsed inward into a pile of rotten planks
covered with ivy. The lone southern wall still stands upright, being the last
sign of the construction. Around the ruins, the landscape has been retaken by
bushes too dense to travel through.
name: Overgrown Ruins

desc:
The sloping landscape is covered with brambles and other shrubs. The surrounding
area can be seen easily from this high perch in the terrain. To the northeast, a
road can be spotted. Further to the east, the border of the dark forest of
Mirkwood fills the whole eastern horizon. A tangled mess of stinging bushes
spreads out to the west and south. Behind the bushes to the far south, a few
high hills are visible in the distance.
name: High Ground

desc:
The wild scrubland descends slightly, but continuously, from the west to the
east. The soil is filled with green shrubbery, although the vegetation does not
rise very high, save a few lone trees. Travel through the plain would be easy,
and one can continue in any direction.
name: Scrubland

desc:
Between the winding slopes lies a small, flat plain with a circular pond in the
centre of it. Green, long grass rustle gently around the pool, some of it
trampled down by the animals wandering in this area. The ground level of the
adjacent areas is slightly higher, forming a natural dell. The bushy scrubland
continues in all directions but to the east, where the vegetation changes into
thick, wild-looking bushes.
name: Pond in the Plains

desc:
The land is uncultivated and covered with sparse stunted undergrowth; the only
exceptions are the small clumps of bushy trees that are growing throughout the
expanse. Between these scattered copses, the vast, wild scrubland extend in all
directions, but to the south, where a huge amount of crude boulders, and dense,
almost-tangled foliage blocks further travel.
name: Scrubland

desc:
The wide scrubland is very flat and seems to extend many miles in all
directions. The ground appears dry, but still quite fertile. Thick, yellow grass
surrounds the holly trees, thistles, and other bushes occupying the area. Wild
weeds grow in abundance across the terrain mixed with a few small trees. Behind
the fields, at the eastern horizon, looms the dark wood of Mirkwood.
name: Bushy Plains

desc:
Man-high, healthy looking bushes have occupied vast areas of the plain. Each
shrub stands alone, having a few yards distance from the other bushes, thus
making the travelling on the flat plain easy, but very unpredictable. The soil
seems fertile: the grass here is taller than in most surrounding areas, and even
some tiny, white flowers grow in small patches among it. The landscape is open
in all directions.
name: Bushy Plains

desc:
The terrain transforms to a peculiar dead end in form of a stony valley filled
with several jagged boulders. It encloses the area, preventing access everywhere
but to the east. The ground is rocky and shattered; many dips and hollows pierce
the earth around the area. In the middle of the valley, a huge, rectangular
boulder with sharp edges rests on top of few others, forming a room-like space
under it.
name: Stony Valley

desc:
Diverse green shrubbery has occupied this area, forming a wide section of dense,
continuous thicket where bushes are rather tall and wide, rich with branches.
The soil is covered with leaves, weeds and other undergrowth. So thick is the
vegetation that it is possible to weave one's way through the copse only where
the brushwood allows it.
name: Thick, Confusing Bushes

desc:
Numerous spike bushes grow on the scrubland, along with a foot high dark green
weed. The thick, impenetrable-looking brushwood continues to the north, while to
the east the landscape is dominated by outskirts of the Mirkwood. To the south,
vegetation turns into grassy plains which seem to extend far into the horizon.
name: Scrublands

desc:
Broad, nearly level stretches of land seem to continue in every direction from
here. Tufted grasses fill the landscape, colouring it with a rich variety of
slightly alternating shades of brown, yellow and green. A few woody plants have
taken root among the spiky bushes that get taller to the eastward. Neither trees
nor boulders stick out from the general blandness.
name: Broad Plains

desc:
These plains are a part of a flat, almost treeless, grassy country. Small bushes
and other woody, rough plants, like briars and thistles, grow here. Green is the
predominant tone of the foliage of these vast grasslands, which extend in all
directions except west, where a steep escarpment, abruptly sinking more than ten
yards down, breaks the mostly even landscape.
name: Verdant Plains

desc:
Rigid, dense grass spreads across the landscape here, cloaking everything in
deep green. The terrain is mostly level, with a few grassy mounds scattered
throughout. The soil looks sunburnt but fertile; among the grass a number of
herbaceous plants are showing new bright green leaves. To the east, a long hedge
of thick bramble bushes separates two grassy plains from each other.
name: Undisturbed Grasslands

desc:
This flowery and fertile land consists of scattered trees within a continuous
vast, flat grassland. The grass has an auburn-tinted hue to it, and on several
spots it appears to have been trampled on. A couple of worn stone boulders are
standing in the sea of grass. Numerous white flowers grow around the rocks,
adorning the area. Lightly rolling mats of grass and forbs stretch onward in
every direction.
name: Auburn Fields

desc:
Lush grasses and small plants have occupied this area. The ground elevates
slightly, creating small mounds covered in green grass with only a few small
bushes with narrow leaves growing on the ground. The general lack of bigger
trees suggests that this is a land of little moisture. The plain continues in
gentle slopes to all directions, granting clear and unobstructed visibility.
name: Mounding Plains

desc:
A beautiful sea of modest heathers dominates the undergrowth, occupying most of
the land surface around the widely spaced, scattered trees. It is coloured with
a rich mixture of deep green leaves, brown stems, and fragile violet blossom. In
addition, blueberries and other woody plant species grow here in abundance,
complementing the scale with blue and more shades of green. Far to the north, a
dark green forest breaks into the horizon and the vegetation gets more bushy.
name: Heather Plains

desc:
A dense thorn barrier separates the scrubland from the dark, sinister Mirkwood.
The ground looks really messy with spiky shrubs mixed with some coarse grass
which grow all over the area. Everything is covered with broken twigs and fallen
leaves which are littering the ground. No signs of wildlife exist, making the
atmosphere silent and oppressing. The thorn barrier continues to the west.
name: Thorn Barrier

desc:
A thick, impenetrable thorn barrier follows the border line of the ancient
forest of the Mirkwood which lies just behind the thorns. The foreboding
presence of the forest hangs in the air and makes even the vegetation look
tainted and grim. Numerous decaying leaves cover the earth, colouring it with
dull shades of brown.
name: Thorn Barrier

desc:
The soil is porous and fertile; a well developed grass stratum and a few trees
of low height grow on it. A wide zone of thick bramble bushes has formed a broad
and tall natural hedge that cuts the passage to the west. The tranquil open
plains continue in other directions, allowing easy and clear travelling. The
ground is filled with small fragrant flowers and plants.
name: Natural Hedge

desc:
A huge, solitary tree stands alone on a small mound; the only break in the vast
expanse of open plains extending to the horizon. Once a truly royal
representative of its species, the tree looks now just old and dried; its uneven
bark has cracked from several spots, and the branches are thin and spindly. A
large brown patch of dead earth surrounds the tree. There, a tiny plant
struggles to survive.
name: A Mighty, Parched Tree

desc:
The Mirkwood is dark, silent and dense. Huge, black trees loom next to each
other; their tangled branches, murky leaves and hanging vines forming a solid
canopy above that is preventing all the light and quickly suffocating all the
sounds. The ground is full of fallen, black leaves, totally hiding the soil
underneath them. A high thorn barrier runs throughout the area, encircling the
dark, silent trees. An uncountable amount of huge spikes is protruding outwards
from the barrier, as a warning of impending death for anyone who dares to
attempt to venture deeper into the forest.
name: Outskirts of Mirkwood

desc:
Perched within the folds of the lonely, parched tree, the thin branches spread
out in all directions. There is scarcely any foliage on the tree, only a few
dry, narrow leaves cling to the tips of the fragile branches. The tree is a good
and obvious vantage point. It offers a clear view of the surrounding lands. The
vast grassland continues in every direction as far as the eye can see except to
the north where the murky Mirkwood looms.
name: Up in a Tree

desc:
The eastern end of the wide plain transforms into a rocky area filled with
stones and boulders of all sizes. A long, bushy cliff stretches through the
area, twisting and branching, forming a confusing sprawl of sheer rock faces,
irregularly shaped boulders, and tangled, dark bushes. In most places, both
visibility and travel is blocked by the eastern boulders.
name: Rocky Area

desc:
The nearer the Mirkwood gets, the denser the brush is. Spine bushes, brambles
and thistles grow in abundance forming a kind of natural passageway which arches
gently towards the west and south. To the north, there is a copse of bushes
which sticks out of its surroundings as the bushes have dried and died where
they stand. To the east and south, one can sense the presence of the dark, huge
forest.
name: Copse of Dried Bushes

desc:
Rustling ivy and periwinkle evoke a sense of uneasiness in these forested hills.
The vines have engulfed several skeletons of great animals. A smell of decay and
death lies heavily on the air. Ruptured tree trunks open up a steep passage
further up onto the hills in the east. In the north the darkness leads into a
murky place.
name: Low Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
Beech, fir and great oaks grow very densely here. Their trunks rise high, aiming
their crowns toward the sky. Most natural light is efficiently blocked out by
the great Mirkwood canopy. A quick fall to the west leads any travellers through
ravaged trunks and vines deeper into the darkness. Downhill in the north and
east the aggressive vegetation leaves just enough space for weary travellers to
continue their exploration.
name: Low Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
The ground makes a steep descent to the south, leaving the peak of the hills
behind and leading into a dense growth of oak, fir and beech. Here the
surroundings are somewhat less overgrown, yet the forest canopy maintains its
density, blocking out all natural light. Just below a great oak tree, a large
bird's nest has fallen and been looted, and is now slowly decaying, a pile of
debris. A slope full of malicious vegetation leads up westwards, deeper into the
gloom.
name: Low Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
The hills are low, with darkened trees leaning over one another. Fir, beech and
oak alternate in regular patterns, together building almost solid walls of trees
-- as though on purpose... The heavy, thick roots of fallen trunks intertwine
with hanging vines to make the going treacherous, with almost no clear way
through for the average traveller. A steep slope to the north climbs into yet
more forested hills, while to the west the forest seems slighly lower.
name: Low Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
An almost fortified forest rises up to the south and east, standing tall and
proud. Decomposing vegetation lies scattered over the forest floor, making
further travel quite demanding, and the malicious vines hanging down from the
branches of the trees leave little room to move. To the north the heavy forest
covers more treacherous hills.
name: Murky Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
Colossal, twisted trees hover over one another, composing a dreadful pattern
with their interwoven branches and foliage. Gnarled, fungi-clad branches and
roots encompass the surrounding, spreading a smell of death and decay. The vile
forest stretches its darkness across the landscape, allowing for few easily
accessible spaces. With some effort the area may be further explored in the
east. In the south Mirkwood opens up onto a minor trail.
name: Dreary Forest

desc:
The corrupted forest displays a scene of twisted trees, bending over one another
in agony. Mossy roots, gnarled and withered, create a treacherous environment,
demanding careful navigation through holes and pits. Periwinkle and ground ivy
grow into a frantic meshwork in the east, blocking any possibility of further
exploration, while in the north small trails and narrow alleys between the trees
allow for investigation.
name: Murky Forest

desc:
The trees ensnare each other with their vast branches and roots, purposefully
creating an almost-impenetrable mesh of vegetation. Many great trees have fallen
heavily to the ground, and are now festering with termites and centipedes. A
faint mist spreads across the forest floor. Traces of strife mark the trunks of
the ancient trees and thorny bushes; but despite being scorched by fire and
wounded by axes and arrows, the forest still stands strong. Dark and dreary
Mirkwood lies open to further exploration to the east and south, while in the
north it turns into an eerie mixture of undergrowth and decay.
name: Murky Forest

desc:
Many trees gape open with vicious wounds, a clear reminder of the evil that
resides within Mirkwood. Fallen vegetation lies decomposed, scattered among the
younger flora, partly covered in ivy, fungi and mosses. Beech and ash create a
dark, grey surrounding. The trees appear to hover over you, closely watching
every move. The forest expands further into the north and south, closely guarded
by the tall shadows of the attentive trees.
name: Eerie Forest

desc:
Two enormous beeches have grown into each other, living in symbiosis. Divided
only at the base, they create a large underground cavern, protected from rain
and wind. Their bark is darkened and withered from old age, with patches of
light grey moss covering it. Malicious fungi infest parts of the old, brittle
roots, adding to the intense, foul smell which spreads across the air. The
never-ending darkness of Mirkwood appears less stifling here. The trail running
through this natural cave continues its path to the east and west.
name: A Trail through a Great Tree

desc:
Oak and beech stand close together, interconnected by periwinkle and ground ivy.
The forest has completely dehydrated the very soil it stands on, leaving the
forest floor dry, brittle and dusty. The imposing darkness may be further
explored in the south and east, while the north is completely blocked by the
dense trees, making it impossible to venture in that direction.
name: Murky Forest

desc:
Fir and beech spread their majestic crowns through the air, efficiently
preventing most natural light from seeping through. Ravaged ground-ivy and
wisteria lie lifeless on the ground. Further up in the trees fungi and mosses
have almost overwhelmed the very trees they get their nourishment from. A slope
descends down to the north, leading deeper into the murky forest of Mirkwood.
name: Low Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
Great birch and beech gather in a great collaborative effort, interweaving their
branches and roots to form an impassable wall in the south and west. A grand
canopy, reinforced by periwinkle and poison ivy, effectively closes out any form
of natural light. The hills appear to come to an end in the east, while in the
north a steep slope leads deeper into the malicious forest of Mirkwood.
name: Murky, Forested Hills

desc:
To the east a small entrance seems to have been purposefully opened between the
great roots of the trees. To the west the forest appears more open and more
readily accessible. An uneasy rustling stemming from the heavy vegetation,
together with the twisted poison ivy and darkened roots, gives the forest an
eerie aura. In the south the forest opens up into ancient, wide plains.
name: Before the Forest Wall

desc:
The light brown earth here is home to patches of grass growing no more than two
feet tall. A burned old farm cart lies in line with an old skeleton of what must
have been an ass or a horse. Far in the east a small trail appears to lead up to
a house; the deserted meadows expand to the south and west. The forest of
Mirkwood stands proud in the north.
name: Deserted Meadows

desc:
The salty, dehydrated ground is littered with pebbles and boulders. Nothing can
be seen growing for several leagues in all directions, except for the great
forest of Mirkwood to the north. The forest springs out of the ground like a
compact castle wall, and no obvious way in can be seen from here. The famished
land stretches further into vast plains to the south, west and east.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
The grass stands almost two feet high, bending to any wind that may blow on it.
The greenery spreads its influence strongly to the south, while the northern
parts of the field appear less fruitful. A scorched fence encircles a burned out
farm in the east, and in the west an esker marks the horizon.
name: Flowing Meadows

desc:
A dusty path almost wholly covered in tussocks of grass lies stretched across
the field. Westward it can barely be made out among the meadows and quickly
disappears in the earthy ground. To the south its contours become more apparent
as the grass grows less abundant. To the north and east the mighty trees of
Mirkwood have created an impassable wall of twisted trunks and vines.
name: A Path in the Fields

desc:
A small, dusty path makes it way to a burned-out farm. The scent of decaying
carcasses befouls the air. There are remainders of what could have been a stable
lying all across the pathway. To the south stands the sooty skeleton of what
appears to have been an old farmhouse. An old fence encircles the farm, and
behind it the plains open up to the west. A heavy brush area grows every so
close to the east, slowly approaching the farm.
name: A Path before a Farm

desc:
The lifeless plains stretch as far as the eye can see, except for the north
where the mighty forest of Mirkwood rises up much like a great wall. The trees
stand aligned, with enormous bushes and shrubs growing between the trunks,
leaving no gaps through which to pass. The ground is covered with rocks of
various sizes, and the dirt on which they lie is slightly white, resembling
salt. Nothing in remote need of nutrients would be able to grow here.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
The meadows are covered with grass, closing in to the ridge stretching from the
north and southwards. Long lines of perfectly rounded pebbles and stones line
the stone ridge. In the north the feet high grass slowly disappears, replaced by
barren fields, and in the south the meadows turn into a vast steppe, while in
the east the undergrowth grows thicker.
name: A Ridge in the Meadows

desc:
A layer of salt covers the entire ground, preventing anything from growing here.
The plains are mostly covered with stones, varying from small pebbles to a
handful of major boulders. Far away in the east the earthy ground appears to be
overwhelmed by rocks, while in the north and south the malnourished plains
expand ruthlessly.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
An ridge disrupts the flat steppe, rising high and steep from the ground.
Rounded pebbles and rocks lie scattered along the stone ridge. Grass has slowly
turned the dried-out surroundings green. The steppe gradually turns into a more
vivid prairie to the east, a flowing meadow to the north, and back to its own
pale self to the west.
name: A Ridge through the Steppe

desc:
A flat, lonely landscape spreads far away towards meadows in the north, and more
plains in the west. The horizon in the east is marked by a heightened esker in
the steppe. The grass here grows to almost one foot in height, and adds a slight
nuance of colour to the otherwise-barren area.
name: Vast Steppe

desc:
A dull, ashen landscape stretches far in all directions. The pale colour of the
earth is due to the layer of salt which covers it, preventing anything from
growing here. Pebbles and rocks lying scattered across the cracked ground are
the only things giving this land shape. A vast steppe opens up to the east.
name: Barren Plains

desc:
The grass stands a few feet tall, growing quite dense. Small bushes and a sole
tree grow here, nourished by the rich soil. The prairie continues in the east,
while in the west the landscape becomes grey, turning into a vast steppe. A
farmhouse has been heavily ravaged, barely standing behind its picket fence in
the north.
name: A Deserted Prairie

desc:
Scrawny trees and bushes of different sizes are slowly taking over more and more
land, disrupting the prevalence of flowing grass. A small snake pit lies poorly
hidden under some rocks, with obvious traces of snakes slithering to and fro the
pit. The vegetation grows thicker in the east and north, while in the west it
appears to be more or less the same as here.
name: A Deserted Prairie

desc:
Great thorn-bushes rise tall to the east, making it close to impossible to move
much further in that direction. To the north the heavy undergrowth gradually
turns into thorny bushes and malicious ground ivy. The brush land slowly turns
into a gentler, greener landscape in the west.
name: Heavy Brushland

desc:
A steady amount of thorns and bushes grows here, reaching towards Mirkwood in
the north and the abundant brush land in the south. A small trail navigates its
way to the west, into vegetation similar to the current surroundings. Small
holes burrow into the ground, leaving entrances and exitways for common field
animals. Rose thorns grow quite tall in the east, making it difficult to move
much further in that direction.
name: Light Brushland

desc:
Undergrowth and foliage are very abundant here, spanning from the south into the
east. Poison ivy uses the burned-out fence in the west as its foundation. In the
north the great forest of Mirkwood leans over the thorny brushland, creating an
impermeable wall of vegetation. An abandoned fox den lies wide open beneath a
clump of shrubs. It appears to have been ravaged by another animal. Remnants of
small animals, doubtless those who fell prey to foxes, lie scattered on the
ground.
name: Light Brushland

desc:
The roof has partly collapsed due to damage from a fire. The southern wall still
stands, and an old skeleton reclines against it. The door is damaged, and is
just barely hanging from its hinges. The walls to the east and north carry what
is left of the ceiling. The vast meadows can be seen through the western window.
Vegetation has slowly started to creep into this area, with vines climbing
through the cracked windows and walls.
name: A Deteriorating Farmhouse

desc:
Great bushes and other foliage are competing for space with the tall grass,
leeching all they can from the poor, dry soil. Small cracks in the field provide
good hunting grounds for spiders and snakes. The majestic Mirkwood forest stands
tall in the east, creating an impenetrable wall, while in the south and west the
brushwood area continues.
name: Heavy Brush Land

desc:
Mirkwood is accessible to the east, through a narrow passage lined by roots,
trunks and vines. Dense thorn-bushes unfold in the west and north, reaching
quite far towards the sky. The north, although it offers only thorns and spines,
appears slightly less intimidating than the east, where the withered beech, oak
and ash of the vast forest rise tall and dark. A light mist is wafting slowly
out of Mirkwood, cloaking everything around, bringing with it a smell of decay.
Hovering over the nearby brush land, the darkness of Mirkwood seems to
attentively watch its surroundings. The darkness appears more treacherous than
anything else.
name: Before Great Mirkwood

desc:
The trees of Mirkwood stand aligned with one another, reaching for the sky.
Their crowns unfold far up in the air, covering every inch of the sky, leaving
the natural light outside. Across the forest floor decaying vines, twigs and
bushes spread an odour of death. The dark forest opens up to more
readily-accessible woods to the north and south.
name: Sinister Forest

desc:
Oak and beech stand tall and proud, their crowns cooperatively forming a vast
canopy, stretching far up into the air. Darkened vines and ivy encircle their
trunks, while heavy vegetation of bushes and roots cover their bases. The ground
is covered in decomposing leaves and twigs. The aggressive vegetation allows for
little exploration, leaving only the north accessible.
name: Sinister Forest

desc:
The threatening, malevolent forest is dark. The sky above cannot be seen through
the net of thick branches, thus eternal darkness encompasses the seemingly
endless, massive trees that tower eerily into the great heights. Tangled,
half-rotten vines hang gloomily down from the twisted tree limbs, here and there
intertwining with the feral, unhealthy looking black bushes. A stench of death
hangs heavily in the air.
name: Sinister Forest

desc:
Thorny vines hang down from the gnarled branches of the trees growing densely
together here. From a decaying corpse, already almost covered with vines and
fallen leaves, spreads a stench of death. The forest has been heavily ravaged in
the east, leaving an open way through the foliage. An eerie gloom imposes itself
from the west; in the north, the forest continues.
name: Mirkwood Forest

desc:
The black, shadowy forest looms in all directions as far as one can see. The
trees are massive, and the big tree trunks are easily more than two yards thick.
The ceiling above is formed by the forest itself, blocking the sky totally out
of the field of vision. Branches twist to and fro, covered by the seemingly
endless vines. The undergrowth looks half rotten, complementing the rather scary
and oppressing atmosphere this place has.
name: Sinister, Still Forest

desc:
A myriad of rotting branches and leaves are spread around, almost covering up
the moss and gravel on the uneven ground. The cramped together trees, nestled
with vines and fallen branches, block further travel in all directions except
for to the east, where the trees seem to grow further apart.
name: Mirkwood Forest

desc:
A great boulder lies at the centre of great swathes of fallen trees and
decomposing thickets. Traces of blood and fur lead towards the boulder. The
forested ground makes an abrupt drop to the south, impossible to traverse. In
the west vines and shrubs grow quite densely between many large, gnarled oaks
and birches.
name: By a Boulder in the Forest

desc:
An open, meadow-like landscape grows mainly brown heather, which have gathered
among the rocks covered by pale green moss, and around the roots of the few
existing trees. Most of the vegetation that covers the ground is dried grass,
although some small plants with glossy, green leaves rise from it. To the west,
a boulder-strewn area can be seen, while in other directions the vegetation
looks more fertile and is flourishing.
name: Plain of Heather

desc:
The surrounding forest stands tall. The fir, beech and oak grow close together,
and their heavy branches and wide crowns engulf Mirkwood in darkness. An old
bear's den has been dug out below the giant roots of an oak, exposing several
cub skeletons. A heavy stench of decay encompasses the area, reinforced by the
moist air. The forest floor slowly rises upwards to the south, leading into
heavily forested hills, while in the north and west the tree trunks and
undergrowth are completely engulfed in darkness.
name: Murky Forest

desc:
The wounded trees of the forest lean their crowns against one other,
collectively supporting the heavy forest roof. The canopy is kept solid by the
dense intertwining of the interweaving vines, boughs and branches. A steep slope
rises to the east while to the west there is a small opening leading into the
darkness.
name: In the Shade of Forested Hills

desc:
Ground ivy makes the forest floor close to impossible to explore. Moving about
requires precise navigation and care. A slope leads slightly upwards in the
east, through ravaged trees and vines. A stench of decay lies heavy over the
area. The dense Mirkwood forest expands its kingdom to the south, into yet
darker, more sombre areas.
name: Low Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
You climb up the dangerous-looking steep slope, grabbing support from black
oozing vines. Alas! The treacherous plants twist under your grip, sending you to
an uncontrolled fall down the dark slope. You hit your head into something and
the gruesome sound of a breaking neck is the last thing you register...
name: A Very Dangerous Slope

desc:
The low hills are slowly turning into a flatter landscape. The uneven, dark soil
appears nutritious, as the flora here is rich. Beech and oak grow rather
densely, yet leave enough room for bushes and vines to claim their presence. The
hills continue their expansion in the north, while the south leads deeper into
the dark forest of Mirkwood.
name: Mirkwood Forest

desc:
The birch and oak reach to staggering heights in the west and south, creating a
fortified, natural wall. The barely discernible north-south trail makes a turn
here, leading east along the forest barrier. A great spider web spans across two
tree-tops. It is littered with dead insects and moths of various sizes. The
remains of a small animal have fallen to the ground, the skeleton almost
completely buried in the dirt. A stench of decay encompasses the whole forest.
To the north the forest opens up into some dark hills.
name: A Dark Corner of Mirkwood

desc:
The massive beeches have grown into each other, separated only by a modest path
at their bases. The grand crowns sway restlessly on the mossy trunks of the
trees. The path makes its way through Mirkwood forest, slowly zigzagging from
the east and extending its way to the west. Great trees stand tall to the south,
blocking any passage in that direction. Mirkwood forest in all its dreariness
opens up for yet another few leagues to the north.
name: A Path along the Forest Wall
